title: Plants: Life & Growth
description: Grade 5 Science: how plants live and grow — photosynthesis, parts of a flower, pollination, from flower to fruit and seed, and how seeds travel. Label the flower and explore.

topics.title: How Plants Make Food
topics.concept:
Green plants make their own food in their leaves. This amazing process is called photosynthesis. To make food, a leaf needs four things:

  • ☀️ Sunlight — the energy.
  • 💧 Water — drawn up by the roots.
  • 💨 Carbon dioxide — a gas taken from the air.
  • 🍃 Chlorophyll — the green colour in leaves that traps sunlight.

The plant makes food (a sugar) and gives out oxygen — the very air we breathe!

recap: Plants make their food in leaves by photosynthesis.
They need sunlight, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll.
Plants give out oxygen — the air we breathe.

wonder.text: Plants never eat a meal, yet they are never hungry. What is their secret food factory?

qa.a: Chlorophyll is the green substance in leaves. It traps the energy in sunlight, which the leaf then uses to make food. That green colour is a plant's super-power!

qa.q: Why are plants so important for us?
qa.a: Plants make the oxygen we breathe and the food we eat. During photosynthesis they take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen — cleaning our air and feeding the world.

topics.title: Parts of a Flower
topics.concept:
A flower has special parts, each with a job in making seeds:

  • 🌸 Petals — bright and scented to attract insects and birds.
  • 🍃 Sepals — small green parts that protect the flower bud.
  • ♂️ Stamen — the male part; it makes a yellow dust called pollen.
  • ♀️ Pistil — the female part in the centre; it receives pollen and makes seeds.

recap: Petals attract insects; sepals protect the bud.
The pistil (female) receives pollen and makes seeds.

wonder.text: A flower is far more than a pretty bloom — it is the plant's way of making new plants. How do its parts work?

qa.q: Why are most flowers brightly coloured?
qa.a: Bright petals and sweet smells attract insects like bees and butterflies. The insects come for nectar and carry pollen between flowers — helping the plant make seeds.

qa.q: Which is the male part and which the female?
qa.a: The stamen is the male part — it makes pollen. The pistil in the centre is the female part — it receives pollen and grows the seeds.

topics.title: Pollination
topics.concept:
Pollination is the moving of pollen from the stamen to the pistil. This must happen before seeds can form. Pollen is carried by:

  • 🐝 Insects — bees and butterflies pick up pollen as they sip nectar.
  • 💨 Wind — blows light pollen from flower to flower.
  • 🐦 Birds and even water can carry pollen too.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 170" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="170" fill="#f2fbf4"/><g fill="#ff8fab"><circle cx="50" cy="70" r="13"/><circle cx="76" cy="70" r="13"/><circle cx="63" cy="56" r="13"/><circle cx="63" cy="84" r="13"/></g><circle cx="63" cy="70" r="9" fill="#FFC93C"/><rect x="60" y="83" width="6" height="50" fill="#2BCB8B"/><g fill="#ffb3c7"><circle cx="224" cy="70" r="13"/><circle cx="250" cy="70" r="13"/><circle cx="237" cy="56" r="13"/><circle cx="237" cy="84" r="13"/></g><circle cx="237" cy="70" r="9" fill="#FFC93C"/><rect x="234" y="83" width="6" height="50" fill="#2BCB8B"/><g stroke="#caa23a" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="5 4" marker-end="url(#poll)"><path d="M90 60 q60 -34 120 0"/></g><defs><marker id="poll" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#caa23a"/></marker></defs><text x="150" y="34" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle">🐝</text><text x="150" y="158" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">A bee carries pollen flower to flower</text></svg>
recap: Pollination moves pollen from stamen to pistil.
It is carried by insects, wind, birds and water.
Bees are very important pollinators for our food.

wonder.text: Pollen made in one flower must reach another to make seeds. But flowers cannot walk — so who delivers the pollen?

qa.a: A bee visits a flower for sweet nectar. Pollen sticks to its furry body. When it flies to the next flower, some pollen rubs off onto that flower's pistil — pollination!
Bees pollinate a huge number of plants, including the ones that give us fruits and vegetables. Without bees, we would have far less food. Bees are tiny heroes!

topics.title: From Flower to Fruit and Seed
topics.concept:
After pollination, the flower changes into a fruit with seeds inside:

  • 🌸 The pollen reaches the pistil and seeds begin to form.
  • 🥀 The petals dry up and fall off.
  • 🍎 The pistil grows into a fruit that holds the seeds.
  • 🌱 Each seed can grow into a brand new plant!

So an apple, a tomato and a pea pod are all fruits that protect seeds.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="160" fill="#f2fbf4"/><g fill="#ff8fab"><circle cx="58" cy="70" r="14"/><circle cx="86" cy="70" r="14"/><circle cx="72" cy="55" r="14"/><circle cx="72" cy="85" r="14"/></g><circle cx="72" cy="70" r="10" fill="#FFC93C"/><g stroke="#2BCB8B" stroke-width="4" fill="none" marker-end="url(#ff)"><line x1="118" y1="75" x2="178" y2="75"/></g><defs><marker id="ff" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#2BCB8B"/></marker></defs><circle cx="232" cy="74" r="34" fill="#ff5a5a" stroke="#d63a3a" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M232 40 q6 -10 14 -8" stroke="#2BCB8B" stroke-width="4" fill="none"/><g fill="#7a3a10"><ellipse cx="222" cy="74" rx="3" ry="6"/><ellipse cx="240" cy="80" rx="3" ry="6"/></g><text x="72" y="130" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#e36b8c" text-anchor="middle">Flower</text><text x="232" y="130" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">Fruit with seeds</text></svg>
recap: After pollination, seeds form and petals fall off.
The pistil grows into a fruit holding the seeds.
Each seed can grow into a new plant.

wonder.text: Watch a flower for a few weeks and the petals fall away — but something new grows in its place. What is it?

qa.a: Yes! In science, a fruit is the part that grows from the flower and holds the seeds. A tomato has seeds inside, so it is really a fruit — even though we cook it like a vegetable.

qa.q: Why does a fruit protect the seed?
qa.a: The fruit keeps the seeds safe as they grow, and often becomes tasty so animals eat it and carry the seeds away — helping new plants grow in new places.

topics.title: How Seeds Travel
topics.concept:
Seeds need to travel away from the parent plant to find their own space, sunlight and water. This is called seed dispersal. Seeds travel by:

  • 💨 Wind — light, fluffy seeds float away (dandelion, drumstick).
  • 💧 Water — seeds that float drift to new shores (coconut).
  • 🐾 Animals — sticky or hooked seeds catch on fur; or animals eat fruit and drop the seeds far away.
  • 💥 Bursting — some pods pop open and fling their seeds out (pea, balsam).
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 130" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="130" fill="#eef9f1"/><g transform="translate(40,10)"><text x="0" y="40" font-size="26">🌬️</text><text x="34" y="40" font-size="22">🌱</text><text x="24" y="100" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5b7" text-anchor="middle">Wind</text></g><g transform="translate(150,10)"><text x="0" y="40" font-size="26">💧</text><text x="34" y="40" font-size="22">🥥</text><text x="24" y="100" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Water</text></g><g transform="translate(250,10)"><text x="0" y="40" font-size="26">🐾</text><text x="34" y="40" font-size="22">🌰</text><text x="24" y="100" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#c96a10" text-anchor="middle">Animals</text></g><text x="165" y="122" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">Seeds travel in many ways</text></svg>
recap: Seed dispersal spreads seeds away from the parent plant.
Seeds travel by wind, water, animals and bursting pods.
Spreading out gives each seed space to grow.

wonder.text: If all seeds fell right under the parent plant, they would crowd and starve. So how do seeds spread far and wide?

qa.a: A coconut has a thick, light husk that floats. It can drift across the sea for a long way and then grow into a new coconut tree on a faraway beach!

qa.q: Why must seeds travel away from the parent?
qa.a: If seeds grew right under the parent plant, they would crowd together and fight for sunlight, water and space. Spreading out gives each seed a better chance to grow.

questions.q: Green plants make their food by…
questions.explanation: Plants make food in their leaves by photosynthesis.

questions.q: The green colour that traps sunlight in leaves is…
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green substance that traps sunlight.
The stamen is the male part that makes pollen.

questions.q: Moving pollen from stamen to pistil is called…
questions.explanation: Pollination is the moving of pollen to the pistil.

questions.q: After pollination, the pistil grows into a…
questions.explanation: The pistil grows into a fruit that holds the seeds.
Light, fluffy dandelion seeds float away on the wind.

questions.q: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and give out…
questions.explanation: Plants give out oxygen — the air we breathe — during photosynthesis.

questions.q: Why are bees so important to us?
options: They pollinate many plants that give us food
questions.explanation: Bees pollinate many food plants; without them we would have far less food.

questions.q: Why is a tomato really a fruit?
options: It grows from the flower and holds seeds
questions.explanation: A fruit grows from the flower and holds seeds — a tomato does both.

questions.q: How does a coconut travel to a new place?
questions.explanation: A coconut's light husk floats, carrying it across water to new shores.

questions.q: Why must seeds travel away from the parent plant?
options: So they don't crowd and can find their own space, light and water
questions.explanation: Spreading out stops crowding and gives each seed space, light and water to grow.
